articles.summary: As of June 14, 2026, measles outbreaks are expanding globally, with Japan reporting a rapid rise in 2026, particularly in the Kanto, Chubu, and Kansai regions. The year-to-date case count already far exceeds the 2025 annual total of 265. Sayaka Takanashi, head of the Vaccination Research Department at the National Institute of Infectious Diseases (NIID), discusses the domestic situation. The article emphasizes the importance of ensuring two-dose measles vaccination to prevent transmission and strengthen population immunity, highlighting vaccination coverage as a key factor in controlling the outbreak.

articles.headlineTranslated: Measles infection in a man in Toyama Prefecture; overseas travel history; since November 2007.
articles.summary: Measles infection reported in a man in his 20s residing in the Takaoka Public Health Center area of Toyama Prefecture, Japan. It is the first measles case in Toyama since November 2019 amid a domestic outbreak. The patient developed fever on the 3rd and visited a Toyama medical facility on the 12th; infection was confirmed by genetic testing at the prefectural Public Health Laboratory and he remains under treatment. He had traveled to Indonesia about three days before onset, an area with higher measles exposure risk. Measles presents with fever and cough and can lead to pneumonia, otitis media, or encephalitis; most patients recover within 7–10 days. Two scheduled routine vaccinations are administered at age 1 and before entering elementary school; authorities urge vaccination to prevent further spread.

The patient developed fever on June 3 and a rash; laboratory confirmation by the Prefectural Institute of Public Health; he is hospitalized. He had recently traveled to Indonesia, where measles transmission is ongoing, and investigators are determining the infection source and transmission route. Measles is highly contagious via airborne and droplet spread; in unimmunized individuals, illness begins with fever and cough, then a high fever (≥39°C) and rash lasting 4–5 days. The contagious period spans from one day before symptom onset to about three days after fever subsides. The prefecture urges caution and advises contacting healthcare facilities by phone before visiting if measles is suspected.

Experts attribute the surge to reduced vaccination during the COVID-19 era and ongoing vaccine hesitancy, lowering population immunity. In context, the article cites Bangladesh as experiencing substantial deaths, illustrating severe outcomes in lower-resource settings. Keywords: vaccination, outbreak, public health measures.

articles.headlineTranslated: Life-threatening risk of severe complications as well... the measles, with its astonishing contagiousness, and the measures to be taken.
articles.summary: Measles is spreading rapidly in Japan and worldwide, driven by its exceptionally high transmissibility (R0 12–18) and airborne spread. A single unimmunized person can infect up to 18 others; in households, about 90% of susceptible contacts become infected. The illness begins with a catarrhal phase (1–4 days) of fever 38–39°C, runny nose, cough and conjunctivitis, followed by a high fever and widespread rash during the eruption phase. Complications include pneumonia and, in about 1 in 1,000 cases, encephalitis; long-term sequelae and SSPE can occur years later. In Japan, outbreaks have surged: 45 cases in 2024, 265 in 2025, and 462 cases by week 18 of 2026 (through May 3), concentrated in urban areas such as Tokyo and Aichi, affecting adults over 20. Vaccination coverage remains below 95% (first dose 92.7%, second dose 91.0% in 2024). An emergency vaccination program for contacts started May 18, 2026. MR vaccine (two doses) offers 97–99% protection; one dose 93–95%.

articles.headlineTranslated: Editorial: Measles Outbreak — Discard the Old Understanding of the Disease
articles.summary: Measles cases rise in Japan, with 498 reported in Tokyo and other cities by May 17, 2026, approaching the 2019 peak of 744. Although not yet confirmed in this prefecture, containment is critical. Measles causes fever, cough, runny nose, and rash about 10 days after exposure and is highly contagious—up to 10 times influenza—with potential encephalitis. There is no specific antiviral therapy. Japan was declared measles-elimination by WHO in 2015, but importations from travelers sustain transmission during a surge. Vaccination remains the most effective defense: one dose ~95% protection; two doses >99%. First-dose coverage fell from ≥95% to 90% in 2024; second-dose has remained below 95% since 2022. Most cases are aged 10–40; those born before 2000-04-01 may lack two doses. Check immunization records, consider antibody testing or voluntary vaccination if uncertain. After the long holiday, cases may rise; contact a provider before visiting if measles is suspected.

articles.summary: Fukuoka City forms Infectious Disease Crisis Management Expert Committee as nationwide measles outbreaks and hantavirus detected on an Atlantic Ocean cruise ship raise concerns. The gathering aligns with concerns over measles activity nationwide and a hantavirus case on an Atlantic cruise ship. On May 25, about 20 healthcare professionals gathered at Fukuoka City Hall to discuss emergency coordination and strengthen information sharing for potential contingencies. Proceedings were closed to the press. This year, nationwide measles cumulative cases reached 479 as of May 13. The meeting underscores local readiness to respond to overseas-origin infectious disease events, with emphasis on inter-agency collaboration and rapid information exchange to prevent and manage outbreaks.

articles.summary: Measles vaccination rates in Fukui Prefecture have fallen below the 95% herd-immunity target, with two-dose MR (measles-rubella) vaccination administered at ages 12–24 months and before entering elementary school (5–7). In 2024, first-dose coverage was 92.6% and second-dose 92.4%; earlier years saw declines (2022 second dose 92.1%; 2023 and 2024 slipping below 95% for the first or second dose). National measles cases reached 479 as of May 13, 2026, the second-highest pace in the past decade after 2019; Fukui has recorded one infection last year and one this year. articles.summary: Measles in Japan surged in 2026, concentrated in the Kanto, Chubu, and Kansai regions, with 479 provisional cases reported in Week 19 (May 4–10) and year-to-date totals already surpassing the 2025 annual figure of 265. Health authorities warn that imported cases appear to have sparked the domestic outbreak, raising questions about how Japan can sustain its measles elimination status. The article quotes Sayaka Takanashi, head of the Vaccination Research Division at the National Institute of Infectious Diseases, who discusses epidemiological trends both domestic and international, and notes that the first installment examines epidemiology while the second will address the role and strategies of measles vaccination. The data indicate ongoing transmission and the need for vigilant surveillance, vaccination coverage, and import-related controls to prevent setback of elimination goals.

articles.headlineTranslated: Five Key Points to Know in Measles Management: 2026 Revised Edition
articles.summary: Measles in Japan continues into 2026, with school-based clusters reported in Aichi Prefecture, Kagoshima Prefecture, and Tokyo. Many cases lack a clear transmission source, increasing vigilance for healthcare facilities about when a measles suspect might present. Keiko Taya of the Kanagawa Prefectural Institute of Public Health outlines five key points for measles management in the revised 2026 edition: (1) early recognition of measles signs in patients presenting to clinics and hospitals, (2) prompt laboratory confirmation, (3) immediate infection control measures to prevent nosocomial spread, (4) rapid public health notification and contact tracing, (5) vaccination considerations for patients and contacts and evaluation of exposure. The update emphasizes ongoing local transmission in addition to imported cases and underscores the need for preparedness in schools and medical settings.
